correctness.rationale: A source and sink at the same vertex are mutually exclusive; at two distinct vertices their joint conditional probability is the product of 2^{-degrees} times (1+edge indicator). Cayley Prüfer degree enumerator and its independently demonstrated weighted-edge derivative yield exact expectations. The pairwise signs follow from Bernoulli inequality and a strict elementary binomial comparison; summing yields the total covariance. An exact similarly marked source-source probability gives the variance. Taylor expansions give the limiting correlation. Complete enumeration through six vertices independently checks all formulas and boundary cases.

value.rationale: Two naturally different association scales have provably opposite signs: every distinct-label source-sink pair is positively correlated but the global source/sink totals are negatively correlated. This resolves a motivated distinction between quenched fixed-tree orientation behavior, which can be positive for a path, and the annealed uniform-labeled-tree ensemble. The exact finite formula and nonzero limiting correlation quantify the effect without arbitrary slicing. No general theorem beyond this natural ensemble is claimed.
